decisions.summary: D2 adopts the inventory's Queue order, which places A1 and R1 among the 'new-question groups' ahead of the wait265 barrier on the premise that they 'touch no fragment 265's unpushed sweeps edited'
decisions.why: The Edge Cases rule is that NO group that edits an existing fragment starts until the clone has 265's landing. R1 edits existing fragments by its own inventory heading ('edits 160-206', inventory.md:131) and A1 edited archetypes 140 and 170-173 (c23242d21), yet both are queued before the barrier on an unmeasured premise. Measured 2026-09-28 (git merge-base --is-ancestor 1c2797c99): the clone lacked 265's close at A1 (c23242d21, 12:40), at R1 (a5adb5994, 13:22) and until the H3 sync-in merge 110004e58 (16:50), five hours after 265 reached main (07:38), because sync.sh exits without merging while the tree is dirty; that merge resolved a conflict on archetypes/170 by keeping A1's side over main's. That is the harm the rule exists to prevent (the request's 'not duplicating work'); nothing made compliance impossible and the GM's words imply no carve-out. Remedy: plan D2 must say that every group editing an existing fragment (A1 and R1 included) waits for the clone - not origin/main - to carry 265's landing, and record A1 and R1 as having run before it; and the fragments A1 and R1 edited are checked against main's side of 110004e58 (archetypes/170 first) so nothing main landed was dropped.
